t: Chinese army captures Shin fortress
c: In 667, the Chinese army crossed the Liao River and captured Shin/Xin Fortress (新城, in modern Fushun, Liaoning).

t: Resistance to Tang rule, population relocated
c: However, there was much resistance to Tang rule (fanned by Silla, which was displeased that Tang did not give it Goguryeo or Paekche's territory), and in 669,…

t: Silla unifies most of Korean peninsula
c: Silla thus unified most of the Korean peninsula in 668, but the kingdom's reliance on China's Tang dynasty had its price.

t: Goguryeo restoration movements begin
c: After the fall of Goguryeo in 668, many Goguryeo people rebelled against the Tang and Silla by starting Goguryeo restoration movements.

t: Tang crowns Bojang king of Joseon
c: In 677, Tang crowned Bojang as the "King of Joseon" and put him in charge of the Liaodong commandery of the Protectorate General to Pacify the East.

t: Dae Jo-yeong establishes Kingdom of Jin
c: Dae Jung-sang and his son Dae Jo-yeong, either a former Goguryeo general or a Mohe chief, regained most of Goguryeo's northern land after its downfall in 668,…

t: Wang Geon establishes Goryeo
c: In 918, Wang Geon overthrew Gung Ye and established Goryeo, as the successor of Goguryeo, and laid claim to Manchuria as Goryeo's rightful legacy.

t: Wang Geon unifies Later Three Kingdoms
c: Wang Geon unified the Later Three Kingdoms in 936, and Goryeo ruled the Korean peninsula until 1392.

t: Koguryo sites become UNESCO World Heritage

t: China and North Korea joint excavation approved
c: North Korea's request to launch a joint excavation project in Northeast China was granted by the PRC government in 1963.

t: China begins Northeast frontier research project
c: In 2002, Chinese government started a five-year research project on the history and current situation of the frontiers of Northeast China which lasted from…

t: Paekche defeated by Tang China and Silla
c: In 660, it was defeated by Tang China and Silla, and ultimately submitted to Unified Silla.

t: King Onjo founds Paekche
c: According to the Samguk sagi, Paekche was founded in 18 BCE by King Onjo, who led a group of people from Goguryeo south to the Han basin.

t: King Gaeru moves Paekche capital north
c: King Gaeru is believed to have moved the capital north of the river to Bukhansanseong in 132, probably in present-day Goyang to the northwest of Seoul.

t: Paekche expansion reaches Gaya confederacy
c: In 249, according to the ancient Japanese text Nihon Shoki, Paekche's expansion reached the Gaya confederacy to its east, around the Nakdong River valley.

t: Paekche defeats Goguryeo at Pyongyang
c: During Geunchogo's reign, the territories of Paekche included most of the western Korean Peninsula (except the two Pyeongan provinces), and in 371, Paekche…

t: King Seong moves Paekche capital to Sabi
c: In 538, King Seong moved the capital to Sabi (present-day Buyeo County), and rebuilt his kingdom into a strong state.

t: Silla-Tang coalition attacks Paekche
c: In 660, the coalition troops of Silla and Tang China attacked Paekche, which was then allied with Goguryeo.

t: Geunchogo pays tribute to Jin dynasty
c: In 372, King Geunchogo paid tribute to the Jin dynasty of China, located in the basin of the Yangtze River.

t: Paekche sends envoys to Song dynasty
c: After the fall of Jin and the establishment of Song dynasty in 420, Paekche sent envoys seeking cultural goods and technologies.

t: Paekche sends envoy to Northern Wei
c: Paekche sent an envoy to Northern Wei of Northern Dynasties for the first time in 472, and King Gaero asked for military aid to attack Goguryeo.

t: Japanese reinforcements arrive at Paekche
c: Additional Japanese reinforcement, including 27,000 soldiers led by Kamitsukeno no Kimi Wakako (上毛野君稚子) and 10,000 soldiers led by Iohara no Kimi (廬原君) also…

t: General Kyŏn Hwŏn establishes Later Paekche
c: In 892, General Kyŏn Hwŏn established Later Paekche, based in Wansan (present-day Jeonju).

t: Later Paekche falls to Goryeo
c: Although Kyŏn Hwŏn rallied the Paekche people and won numerous victories against Silla and Goryeo, Later Paekche later fell in 936 to King Taejo of Goryeo.

t: Baekje Cultural Land opened to visitors
c: In 2010, Baekje Cultural Land was opened to visitors.

t: Baekje Historic Areas designated UNESCO World Heritage Site
c: Baekje Historic Areas, which feature locations with remains of the period, was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2015.

t: Jijeung standardizes Silla characters
c: In 504, Jijeung of Silla standardized the characters into 新羅 (신라), which in Modern Korean is pronounced Silla.

t: Silla founded by Bak Hyeokgeose
c: According to Korean records, Silla was founded by Bak Hyeokgeose of Silla in 57 BCE, around present-day Gyeongju.

t: Liberation of Korea

t: Pasa of Silla conquers Eumjipbeol
c: In response, Pasa of Silla invaded Eumjipbeol in 102 and Tachugan surrendered, and the Siljikgok and Apdok, which were frightened by Silla, also surrendered.

t: Goguryeo moves capital to Pyongyang
c: When Goguryeo began to expand its territory southward, moving its capital to Pyongyang in 427, Nulji of Silla was forced to ally with Paekche.

t: Silla annexes Geumgwan Gaya
c: Silla absorbed the Kaya confederacy during the Kaya–Silla Wars, annexing Geumgwan Gaya in 532 and conquering Daegaya in 562, thereby expanding its borders to…

t: Silla breaks alliance and takes Han River
c: Silla helped Paekche drive Goguryeo out of the Han River (Seoul) area, and then wrested control of the entire central western Korea region from Paekche in 553,…

t: Silla-Tang alliance conquers Goguryeo
c: In 668, under King Munmu of Silla (King Muyeol's successor) and General Kim Yu-sin, the Silla–Tang alliance conquered Goguryeo to its north after the…

t: Queen Jindeok, last sacred bone ruler, dies
c: This duality had ended when Queen Jindeok, the last ruler from the "sacred bone" class, died in 654.

t: Gyeongju added to UNESCO World Heritage
c: The historic area around Gyeongju was added to the UNESCO World Heritage list in 2000.

t: Hahoe and Yangdong Folk Villages submitted for UNESCO heritage
c: Additionally, two villages near Gyeongju named Hahoe and Yangdong Folk Village were submitted for UNESCO heritages in 2008 or later by related cities and the…

t: Buddhism adopted by Three Kingdoms states
c: In Korea, it was adopted as the state religion of 3 constituent polities of the Three Kingdoms Period, first by Goguryeo in 372 CE, by Silla in 528 CE, and by…

t: Samguk Sagi chronicle compiled
c: Samguk Sagi— the official chronicle of the Three Kingdoms era, compiled in 1145—contains further descriptions of commercial items sold by Middle Eastern…

t: Emperor Gaozong sends message to Paekche
c: In 651, Emperor Gaozong of Tang sent a message to the king of Paekche referring to the Three Kingdoms of Korea as Samhan.

t: Buddhism introduced to Paekche from Goguryeo
c: Buddhism was introduced to Paekche in 384 from Goguryeo, which Paekche welcomed.

t: Kaya confederacy emerges
c: The Kaya confederacy was a confederacy of small kingdoms in the Nakdong River valley of southern Korea since 42 CE, growing out of the Byeonhan confederacy of…

t: Three Han commanderies established in Korea
c: When Old Chosŏn was defeated in 108 BCE, three commanderies were established in its place: Lelang, Lintun, and Zhenfan.

t: Xuantu Commandery established
c: In 107 BCE, Xuantu Commandery was also established in the place of Gojoseon's ally, Yemaek.

t: Lintun and Zhenfan absorbed into larger commanderies
c: In 82 BCE, Lintun was absorbed into Xuantu and Zhenfan absorbed into Lelang.

t: Gongsun Du appointed Administrator of Liaodong Commandery
c: Gongsun Du was appointed Administrator of Liaodong Commandery by Dong Zhuo in 189 on the recommendation of Xu Rong.

t: Death of Gongsun Du, succession of Gongsun Kang
c: Du died in 204 and was succeeded by his son, Gongsun Kang.

t: Gongsun Kang expands into Goguryeo, creates Daifang
c: In 204 Kang expanded into Goguryeo and created Daifang Commandery.

t: Yuan Shang and Yuan Xi flee to Gongsun Kang
c: When the Wuhuan were defeated by Cao Cao in 207, Yuan Shang, Yuan Xi, and the Wuhuan leaders Louban and Supuyan fled to Kang.

t: Goguryeo moves capital east to Hwando region
c: Gongsun Kang took some territory in 209 and Goguryeo was forced to move its capital further east to the Yalu rivery valley near Hwando.

t: Death of Gongsun Kang, succession of Gongsun Gong
c: Kang died in 220 when his children were too young to rule, so his brother Gongsun Gong succeeded him.

t: Gongsun Yuan succeeds Gongsun Gong
c: Gong became ill and was replaced by his nephew Gongsun Yuan in 228.

t: Sima Yi invades and annexes Liaodong territory
c: Yuan ruled independently until Sima Yi invaded in 238 and annexed his territory.

t: Goguryeo allies with Cao Wei against Liaodong
c: In 238, Goguryeo allied with Cao Wei to overthrow the Liaodong regime.

t: Goguryeo raids Xuantu Commandery
c: Goguryeo raided the Xuantu Commandery in 242.

t: Cao Wei invades Goguryeo
c: In retaliation, Cao Wei invaded Goguryeo from 244 to 245.

t: Jin dynasty loses Lelang Commandery
c: Lelang Commandery was ruled by the Jin dynasty until 313.

t: Dong Shou flees Former Yan to Goguryeo
c: Dong Shou was a general from Former Yan who fled to Goguryeo in 336 and was given a position in the former territory of Lelang.

t: Harvard Early Korea Project loses funding

t: Samhan formed after Old Chosŏn collapse
c: The Samhan are thought to have formed around the time of the fall of Old Chosŏn in northern Korea in 108 BCE.

t: Gojong establishes Korean Empire
c: In 1897, Gojong changed the name of Joseon to the Korean Empire, Daehan Jeguk, in reference to the Three Kingdoms of Korea.

t: Korean provisional government declares Republic of Korea
c: In 1919, the provisional government in exile during the Japanese occupation declared the name of Korea as the Republic of Korea, Daehan Minguk, also in…

t: Memorial stone discovered in Cheongju
c: In 1982, a memorial stone dating back to 686 was discovered in Cheongju with an inscription: "The Three Han were unified and the domain was expanded." During…

t: King Jun establishes Mahan in southern Korea
c: One of the most prominent leaders of the Han (Korean: 한; 韓) Immigration was King Jun of Old Chosŏn from the northern Korea, having lost the throne to Wiman,…

t: Buyeo establishes ties with Han Xuantu Commandery
c: In the later Western Han, Buyeo established close ties with the Xuantu Commandery, one of Four Commanderies of Han, according to volume 85 of the Book of the…

t: Buyeo becomes tributary of Liaodong
c: When Emperor Xian ruled Eastern Han, Buyeo was reclassified as a tributary of the Liaodong Commandery of Han.

t: Murong Hui invades Buyeo, King Uiryeo suicides
c: In 285 the Murong tribe of the Xianbei, led by Murong Hui, invaded Buyeo, pushing King Uiryeo (依慮) to suicide, and forcing the relocation of the court to Okjeo.

t: Buyeo pays tribute to Northern Wei
c: Buyeo paid tribute to Northern Wei in 457–8 and accompanied a Wuji mission to Wei in 486.

t: Damolou sends tribute missions to Northern Qi
c: The Book of Northern Qi records two tribute missions from Damolou in 567 and 569 but the History of the Northern Dynasties completed in 659 notes that contact…

t: Damolou leads final tribute mission
c: The New Book of Tang records a final tribute mission by Damolou in 723 along with the Dagou (Shiwei) people.

t: King Dongmyeong attacks Northern Okjeo
c: In 28 BCE, King Dongmyeong sent Bu Wiyeom to attack the Northern Okjeo.

t: Paekche leads Sabi Conferences
c: In 541 and 544, Paekche led the Sabi Conferences (泗沘會議), which were participated in by seven countries including Ara.

t: Japan-South Korea historians agree Kaya was not colonized
c: In 2010, a joint study group of historians sponsored by the governments of Japan and South Korea agreed that Kaya had never been militarily colonized by…

t: Migration follows Wiman Chosŏn collapse
c: Further migration followed after the fall of Wiman Chosŏn and establishment of the Chinese commanderies in the Korean peninsula region in 108 BCE.

t: King Chun flees to Jin and establishes polity
c: According to the Book of the Later Han of ancient China, King Chun of the kingdom of Kija Chosŏn (second dynasty of Old Chosŏn allegedly founded by Jizi/Kija),…

t: King Munmu attacks Baekje
c: In 660, King Munmu ordered his armies to attack Baekje.

t: Khitan Liao dynasty conquers Parhae
c: Parhae was conquered by the Khitan-led Liao dynasty in 926.

t: Tae Choyŏng founds Kingdom of Jin
c: Parhae was founded in 698 by Tae Choyŏng (Da Zuorong) under the name 震 (진, Jin), read as tsyinH in Middle Chinese.

t: Tae Choyŏng settles in Yingzhou
c: According to Old Book of Tang, after Goguryeo was defeated by the Tang, Tae Choyŏng (Da Zuorong) led his relatives to settle in Yingzhou (營州, modern-day…

t: Tae Choyŏng declares himself king
c: In 698, Tae Choyŏng declared himself King of Zhen (Jin).

t: Mohe chieftains move east during Khitan rebellion
c: In 696, three Mohe chieftains took advantage of the Khitan rebellion to move further east.

t: Tang recognizes Tae Choyŏng as Prince of Bohai
c: In 713 or 714, the Tang dynasty recognized Tae Choyŏng as the "Prince of Bohai (Parhae)", the name for the sea surrounding Liaodong and Shandong.

t: Sogdian population in Parhae increases sharply
c: After the defeat of the An Lushan rebellion in 763, the number of Sogdians in Parhae increased sharply.

t: Uyghurs flee to Parhae after Khaganate collapse
c: However, after the destruction of the Uyghur Khaganate in 840, many Uyghurs fled to Parhae but failed to adapt to Parhae society and caused social unrest.

t: Death of Tae Choyŏng
c: Tae Choyŏng died in 719 and was succeeded by his son, Tae Muye Da Wuyi, r.

t: Emperor Daizong formally recognizes Parhae as state
c: In 762, Emperor Daizong of Tang formally recognized Parhae as a state and Hŭmmu as its king.

t: Heishui Mohe seeks peace with Silla
c: In 886, the Heishui Mohe put up wooden signs declaring that they wished to establish peaceful relations with Silla.

t: Silla builds defensive wall against Parhae
c: Silla did not advance beyond the Taedong River and in 827, Silla mobilized 10,000 people to build a defensive wall along the river due to attacks from Parhae.

t: Parhae attacks Khitans after Liaoy fallang
c: Only after 918, when the Khitans took Liaoyang and resettled its people did Parhae respond with an attack in 924.

t: Parhae conflicts with Khitan Liao dynasty

t: Last Parhae resistance destroyed
c: The last remnants of Parhae resistance from the former state of Chŏngan were destroyed by 999.

t: Taejo stages Manbu Bridge Incident against Liao envoys
c: The Liao dynasty sent 30 envoys with 50 camels as a gift in 942, but Taejo exiled the envoys to an island and starved the camels under a bridge, in what is…

t: Dongdan Kingdom abolished, Parhae integrates into Liao

t: Rebellion at Eastern Capital under Xiao Baoxian
c: In 1116 another rebellion occurred at the Eastern Capital when the Khitan Regent Xiao Baoxian alienated the population due to his harsh administration.

t: Parhae capital moved to Helong
c: In 742 it was moved to the Central Capital in Helong, Jilin.
